category_title: Struggling readers who forget intended dictation during technology delays
minimal_context: David is at the writing center using the Dragon Speech Recognition app on an iPad to dictate his own version of a patterned story.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's write your version of the Brown Bear story on the iPad. Press the button to dictate your sentence about the Transformer.

STUDENT: (Touches the dictation button and goes blank) I want to write... um...

TUTOR: What do you think you should say?

STUDENT: I see a Transformer driving by me. (Looks at the screen) The app timed out.

TUTOR: Try pressing the button and saying it again.

STUDENT: (Repeats the process three times) It typed the wrong words again! (Deletes the entire sentence) I don't want to do this anymore.

options.A: Dictate the composition to the speech recognition app, show the student the transcription, discuss its accuracy, and refer to it while writing the composition on chart paper.
options.B: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the dictation task before the speech recognition app times out during the writing center block.
options.C: Pay attention to the student's avoidance strategies as compensations for the cognitive load rather than refusals to comply with the expected dictation task.
options.D: Alter how the behavior is interpreted during the writing block, viewing the student's frustration as a desire for social interaction rather than simple noncompliance.
